newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fortis repeats on buy lookout.
newsitem.headline: Fortis repeats on buy lookout.

text.p: Belgian-Dutch financial group Fortis is still on the lookout for acquisitions which would strengthen its market positions in a number of countries, group co-chairman Maurice Lippens said in a magazine interview.

"In France, Australia or in Britain we are present without having critical mass, but we remain always receptive to opportunities that would allow us to achieve it," Lippens told the March edition of "Crescendo", a magazine published by Belgian telephone company Belgacom SA for its clients.
Fortis is co-owned by Fortis AG and Fortis AMEV .
Fortis has said repeatedly it looks at all opportunities that are presented to it, although generally declines to comment on specific rumours or cases.
Fortis was recently linked to a bidding war for Scottish mutual insurance company Scottish Amicable, although the company later denied it was interested in making an offer.

Last year the group completed the acquisition of Dutch merchant bank MeesPierson and is presently negotiating with the Belgian government about raising its 49.9 percent stake in Belgian bank ASLK-CGER.
Lippens was quoted in Crescendo as saying the company had achieved critical mass in Belgium, a "quasi"-critical mass in the Netherlands and in small niches in other markets.
Fortis said on Wednesday it would release 1996 results at 1500 local (1400 GMT) on March 26.
